content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Daniel Gutierrez (E046) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory has two conflicting notes:

Note 1: role Payroll Specialist, employment type full_time, recommendation write. Comment says full-time Payroll Specialist, requested write which is at allowed maximum for full-time employees in a system owned by their role. Recommend granting write.

Note 2: employment type contractor, security training basic, role Payroll Specialist, recommendation read. Comment says contractor with basic security training, max read. Requested write exceeds max, so recommend read. Notes conflict with prior note; security record indicates contractor.

So there is a conflict: HR says full_time, Security says contractor.

Access policy:
1. full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if role owns system.
2. contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

If full_time: requested write ≤ max write → grant write.
If contractor with basic training: max read → grant read.

Which to trust? The security record indicates contractor. Hmm. The Approver should make the final decision based on the information. We have two conflicting facts. Which one is more reliable? The Security note explicitly says "security record indicates contractor" and notes the conflict. The security DB is typically the authoritative source for employment/access eligibility.

The policy says contractor read or write if advanced security training. Security training basic → max read. So grant read.

I'll go with read, citing the conflicting evidence and that security record indicates contractor with basic training, so maximum is read, and the requested write exceeds it.

Submit decision: read.
